title: Blue Horde
capsule: The Blue Horde was the eastern wing of the Golden Horde, the Mongol successor state on the western Eurasian steppe founded after Batu Khan's withdrawal from Europe in 1242, with its heartland between the Volga and Ural rivers. Historians debate which half of the Golden Horde the label designates, owing to conflicting Turkic and Persian color-direction conventions, but the term is conventionally applied to the left-wing ulus centered east of the Volga. The combined Golden Horde reached its zenith under Uzbeg Khan (r. 1313–1341), who imposed Islam on the polity and conducted sustained warfare against the Ilkhanate. After the Black Death and Tokhtamysh's reunification attempt, the structure fragmented; by 1449 the Blue Horde's distinct political identity had dissolved into successor khanates.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Blue Horde specifically is poorly delineated in primary sources; most boundary reconstructions are conjectural, extrapolated from the better-documented Golden Horde as a whole and known garrison points along the Volga and Ural rivers.
